A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 18 pages of each version, including Appendices A–F, are readable, and corresponding text, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments generating 2,268 PerDisNews texts, evaluating personalization and safety, validating judgments with human annotations, and measuring detectability.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and reports expanded human annotation and revised validation results.

M1.justification: The generation models, three personalization prompt types, automatic evaluation procedures, and detection methods are unchanged. Expanding the human validation panel changes evaluation settings rather than the underlying method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same six narratives, seven target groups, English-language PerDisNews corpus, external validation/calibration datasets, and five combined-profile showcases in Appendix E. Additional annotators do not introduce new task coverage.

E2.justification: The same six generators, three LLM judges, and no-personalization control remain. Detection comparisons retain Gemma-2-9b-IT, Detection-Longformer, and Binoculars, including in the relocated calibration table.

E3.justification: Sections 3 and 5.2 increase human ratings from two to five per text for the unchanged 109-text validation subset. Appendix D also changes its stated reference average from two to five human annotations while retaining its correlations; this establishes a reported setting change, but not that this separate validation was rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 expands the annotator-level diagnostic comparison to Human3–Human5 and discusses differences in score-use tendencies. Existing prompt comparisons, target-group analyses, combined-profile showcases, and detector breakdowns remain.

E5.justification: Two-rater agreement reporting becomes averaged agreement across five raters, with separate unanimous and majority agreement statistics. The existing three generated samples per condition and detector significance-testing procedures are retained.

E6.justification: With the expanded human reference, human–LLM correlation changes from 0.75 to 0.76 and mean absolute error from 0.51 to 0.45. Human agreement changes from two-rater correlation 0.70 to average correlation 0.62, with additional annotator and majority-agreement results. These are revised validation results under changed conditions; linguistic-quality and detection scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The personalization scoring scale and narrative-stance definitions remain unchanged. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions, proofs, or mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about personalized disinformation generation, reduced safety-filter activation, usable LLM-based evaluation, and slightly reduced detectability. The larger annotation panel supplies revised support without changing these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations remain substantively unchanged, including uncertainty about causal explanations, English-only applicability, restricted narrative coverage, and imperfect evaluation of personalization quality. Newly described annotator tendencies are observational results.

D1.justification: Footnote 1 changes analysis-code and request-based dataset release from forthcoming to reported availability. Section 3 explicitly identifies two annotators for the existing 50-text guideline pilot. Generation hyperparameters and Appendix B computational resources remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference lists contain the same works, and the positioning relative to previous personalization, disinformation-generation, and detection research is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes small abstract language corrections, locally revises human-validation descriptions, updates cross-references, and shortens the supplementary-data overview after relocating displays. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v1 Tables 6 and 7 move into the main text as v2 Tables 2 and 4. Figures 12 and 13 similarly become Figures 5 and 7; the annotation plot adds three human rows. Other figure graphics are unchanged, with renumbering and reflow within the retained two-column layout.

improvement.justification: Expanding validation from two to five annotators reduces dependence on two individuals, while relocating relevant evidence into the main text improves accessibility. The gain is limited by the unchanged 109-text, author-only validation sample. A new apparent reporting error—the '0.29%' agreement figure in Section 5.2—reduces clarity but does not outweigh these modest benefits.
